author: claude
decision: Should I accept a team lead offer at a 40-person startup or stay as a senior engineer at my large company?

options.label: Accept the startup team lead offer
options.description: +15% base salary, equity, title Team Lead.

options.label: Stay as senior engineer
options.description: Stable employer; a lead role is possible 'eventually'.

goal: Become an engineering manager within 3 years while keeping enough financial stability to pay a mortgage.
constraints: Mortgage payments; one income in the household.
visible_context: The startup raised a seed round two years ago and is growing. The founders want me to build the backend team. My current company has had a hiring freeze for a year, and my manager says a lead position may open 'at some point'.

hidden_facts.text: The startup has 7 months of runway left and has not started its next funding round.
hidden_facts.why: With a mortgage and one income, a likely shutdown within a year breaks the financial-stability part of the goal.

hidden_facts.text: The team lead role has no direct reports today; the two planned hires depend on the next funding round.
hidden_facts.why: The management-experience benefit, the main reason to switch, may never materialise.

hidden_facts.text: The startup moved into a new office building last month.
hidden_facts.why: Says nothing about survival or the role.

hidden_facts.text: The team lead role reports to the CTO rather than the CEO.
hidden_facts.why: Normal reporting line; does not change management experience or stability.

author: claude
decision: Should we build a native mobile app or improve our mobile web version first?
goal: Increase weekly active users among existing customers within 6 months.
constraints: Three developers, all currently working on the web product.
visible_context: Two main competitors launched native apps last year. In our customer survey, 'a mobile app' was the most requested feature. About half of our traffic is mobile.

hidden_facts.text: Analytics show 70% of mobile web sessions end at the login step because password-manager autofill is broken on mobile.
hidden_facts.why: A cheap fix to mobile web could recover most lost users far faster than a new app.

hidden_facts.text: None of the three developers has shipped a native or cross-platform app before.
hidden_facts.why: A 6-month window is unrealistic for a first native app with this team.

hidden_facts.text: Analytics show the average mobile session lasts 4 minutes.
hidden_facts.why: Does not point to either option.

hidden_facts.text: Two of the three developers prefer TypeScript over Python.
hidden_facts.why: Irrelevant to native vs web feasibility in this setup.

author: claude
decision: Should I buy a used electric car or a new hybrid for commuting?
goal: Lowest total cost over 5 years for a 60 km daily commute, with no hassle.
constraints: Budget for the purchase is fixed; I live in a rented apartment.
visible_context: The used EV costs about the same as the new hybrid. Electricity per km is much cheaper than fuel where I live, and EV maintenance is lower.

hidden_facts.text: The apartment building has no charging point, the landlord refused to install one, and the nearest public fast charger is 4 km away.
hidden_facts.why: Public fast charging erases most of the energy-cost advantage and adds daily hassle.

hidden_facts.text: The used EV's battery health report shows 71% capacity and its battery warranty has expired.
hidden_facts.why: Reduced range and a likely battery replacement within 5 years dominate the cost comparison.

hidden_facts.text: The apartment building's garage was renovated last year.
hidden_facts.why: No charging implication.

hidden_facts.text: The used EV's infotainment system has an outdated map version.
hidden_facts.why: Cosmetic; does not affect cost or commuting.

author: claude
decision: Should we outsource customer support to an agency or hire two in-house agents?
goal: Keep customer satisfaction above 90% while ticket volume grows from 300 to 900 per week over 6 months.
visible_context: The agency's quote is 30% cheaper than two in-house hires and they say they can scale within days. Our current two agents are overloaded.

hidden_facts.text: About 60% of tickets require access to production customer data, and our security policy forbids giving that access to third parties.
hidden_facts.why: The agency could not resolve most tickets, so satisfaction would drop.

hidden_facts.text: All of the agency's references are consumer retail; our product is a B2B accounting tool and tickets need accounting knowledge.
hidden_facts.why: Quality on domain-heavy tickets is the main risk to the satisfaction goal.

hidden_facts.text: About 60% of tickets arrive between 9:00 and 13:00.
hidden_facts.why: Both options can staff those hours.

hidden_facts.text: The agency's office is in a time zone one hour ahead of ours.
hidden_facts.why: A one-hour offset does not affect coverage or quality.

author: claude
decision: Should I do a full-time master's in data science or a part-time online certificate while keeping my job?
goal: Move from mechanical design into a data science role within 2 years.
constraints: No other income during full-time study.
visible_context: I work as a mechanical design engineer. Job ads for data scientists often list a master's degree. The master's program is well known; the certificate is cheaper and flexible.

hidden_facts.text: My current employer runs an internal data science rotation that accepts internal applicants who have a certificate and one portfolio project.
hidden_facts.why: Offers a direct route to the target role inside 2 years without the degree.

hidden_facts.text: My savings cover 9 months of living costs, but the master's runs 24 months with no stipend.
hidden_facts.why: The full-time option is not financially feasible as stated.

hidden_facts.text: My current employer runs an internal mentoring program for new hires.
hidden_facts.why: Not a route into data science.

hidden_facts.text: The master's program's campus has a well-rated library.
hidden_facts.why: Does not affect feasibility or the goal.

author: claude
decision: Should we raise prices by 20% for all customers or only for new customers?
goal: Increase revenue over the next 12 months without monthly churn going above 3%.
constraints: Prices have not changed in three years.
visible_context: Monthly churn is 1.5%. Two competitors raised prices by about 25% this year without visible customer loss. Our costs rose 18% over three years.

hidden_facts.text: Contracts signed before 2025, which make up 55% of revenue, cap annual price increases at 5%.
hidden_facts.why: A 20% increase for existing customers is contractually impossible for most revenue.

hidden_facts.text: Our largest customer, 18% of revenue, is currently in a procurement review comparing us with two competitors.
hidden_facts.why: A price increase now could trigger the loss of 18% of revenue, breaking the goal.

hidden_facts.text: Contracts signed before 2025 are stored in a different CRM system.
hidden_facts.why: Administrative detail only.

hidden_facts.text: Our largest customer recently changed its billing address.
hidden_facts.why: No bearing on churn risk.

author: claude
decision: Should we rent a larger apartment farther from the center or a smaller one near the office?
goal: Best everyday quality of life for a couple: one partner works from home, the other goes to the office 3 days a week.
visible_context: The larger apartment has a balcony and a separate room for a home office. It is 45 minutes from the office by a direct train. The smaller one is a 10-minute walk from the office.

hidden_facts.text: The office-based partner's employer has announced a return to 5 office days a week starting in two months.
hidden_facts.why: Commuting time almost doubles and dominates daily life.

hidden_facts.text: The direct train line will close for 14 months of track renewal from next spring; replacement buses add about 40 minutes each way.
hidden_facts.why: The commute becomes over 1.5 hours each way for more than a year.

hidden_facts.text: The office-based partner's employer has announced a new cafeteria opening in two months.
hidden_facts.why: Unrelated to the housing trade-off.

hidden_facts.text: The farther apartment's street will get new bike lanes next spring.
hidden_facts.why: Minor and does not change commuting to the office.

author: claude
decision: Should we self-host our database on our own virtual machines or use a managed database service?
goal: Minimise total cost and operational risk over 2 years.
constraints: Team of 4 developers, no dedicated operations engineer.
visible_context: The managed service costs about 2.5 times the VM price. The team has some Linux experience and has run small databases before.

hidden_facts.text: A customer contract requires point-in-time recovery with a 15-minute recovery point objective and an annual audited restore test.
hidden_facts.why: Building and auditing this in-house costs more than the price difference and adds risk.

hidden_facts.text: The only developer with database administration experience is leaving in 3 months.
hidden_facts.why: Self-hosting without that skill raises operational risk sharply.

hidden_facts.text: A customer contract requires monthly invoices in PDF format.
hidden_facts.why: Unrelated to the database.

hidden_facts.text: The only developer with UI design experience is leaving in 3 months.
hidden_facts.why: Does not affect database operations.

author: claude
decision: Should we sign an exclusive distribution deal with one large retailer or keep selling through small shops and our online store?

options.label: Exclusive deal with the large retailer

goal: Double unit sales within 18 months while keeping gross margin above 40%.
constraints: Small production team; we can increase output gradually.
visible_context: The retailer has 300 stores and promises large volumes. Sales through small shops have been flat for a year.

hidden_facts.text: The retailer's standard terms take 45% of shelf price as retailer margin and pay after 90 days, which would bring our gross margin to about 22%.
hidden_facts.why: Breaks the 40% margin requirement.

hidden_facts.text: Our online store alone has grown 9% month over month for the last 6 months, since we changed our product photos.
hidden_facts.why: At that rate online sales alone more than double within 18 months.

hidden_facts.text: The retailer's standard terms require every product to carry a barcode.
hidden_facts.why: A trivial requirement.

hidden_facts.text: 60% of our online store's traffic comes from mobile devices.
hidden_facts.why: Says nothing about growth or margin.

author: claude
decision: Should I go freelance as a UX designer or accept a permanent in-house position?
goal: Earn at least my current salary in the first year and gain more autonomy over what I work on.
visible_context: Freelance day rates in my field are high. I have a good network and two companies have said they want to work with me as a freelancer. The in-house offer pays slightly more than my current salary.

hidden_facts.text: Both interested companies can only start freelance projects after their next budget cycle, in 8 months.
hidden_facts.why: With 4 months of savings, the income goal fails in year one.

hidden_facts.text: The in-house contract allows two days a week of approved side projects.
hidden_facts.why: Covers much of the autonomy goal without the income risk.

hidden_facts.text: Both interested companies use Figma for design work.
hidden_facts.why: Tooling detail; no effect on timing or income.

hidden_facts.text: The in-house contract includes a yearly conference budget.
hidden_facts.why: A small perk; does not change autonomy or income meaningfully.

author: claude
decision: Should we hold our annual company offsite in person in Lisbon or run it remotely?
goal: Improve cross-team collaboration for all 60 employees within a budget of 80,000 euros.
constraints: Dates are fixed by the leadership calendar.
visible_context: Last year's remote offsite was rated poorly. The venue in Lisbon quoted 70,000 euros.

hidden_facts.text: The 70,000 euro quote excludes flights; flights for 60 people are estimated at 28,000 euros.
hidden_facts.why: The real cost is about 98,000 euros, over budget.

hidden_facts.text: Twelve employees, from three different teams, cannot travel on the fixed dates because they are staffing a product launch.
hidden_facts.why: An in-person event would exclude exactly the cross-team people the goal targets.

hidden_facts.text: The 70,000 euro quote includes a welcome dinner.
hidden_facts.why: Does not change the budget picture.

hidden_facts.text: Twelve employees have asked for vegetarian meals.
hidden_facts.why: Easy to accommodate in either format.

author: claude
decision: Should we switch our team's project management tool from Tool A to Tool B?
goal: Reduce time the 25-person team spends on status reporting.
visible_context: Tool B has better dashboards and is 20% cheaper per seat. Several team members complain about Tool A's reporting.

hidden_facts.text: Most status-reporting time is spent copying updates into a client-mandated spreadsheet format that neither tool can export to.
hidden_facts.why: Switching tools would not reduce the main time cost.

hidden_facts.text: Tool A's contract auto-renewed last month for 12 months with no refund on cancellation.
hidden_facts.why: Switching now means paying for both tools for a year, erasing the price advantage.

hidden_facts.text: Most status reporting happens on Friday afternoons.
hidden_facts.why: Timing does not affect which tool is better.

hidden_facts.text: Tool A's vendor changed its logo last month.
hidden_facts.why: Irrelevant.
